Known science foundations of Matter-to-Product Fabrication System.

CNC, 3D printing, and robotic assembly convert digital designs to parts worldwide. Lights-out factories (e.g., FANUC) run with minimal human presence. Digital twins verify designs before fabrication. The frontier is generality: handling arbitrary verified designs without human process engineering.

Key quantity check (Lights-out factory uptime in hours per human intervention / traditional cell): computed ratio 90 against the reference value, relative error 0, within the stated tolerance of 0.3. This calculation was executed in Node.js at build time and the output stored verbatim.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

Physical and engineering constraints on Matter-to-Product Fabrication System.

Arbitrary designs still need human process planning. Verification of designs against manufacturing constraints is incomplete. Multi-material, multi-process products need coordination across machines.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 4 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is additive build rate vs robotic cell count worldwide at 4 orders of magnitude (robotic cell count worldwide larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.
